text: . Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal today called upon the youth of the country to embrace emerging technologies, continuously upgrade their skills and contribute to India’s journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047. He also called upon young people to prepare for the changing employment landscape by developing skills in AI, cybersecurity and the practical application of emerging technologies.  The Minister  made these remarks while addressing the inauguration of the SRCC Centenary Conclave on Pathways to Viksit Bharat in New Delhi.The Minister emphasised that investments in manufacturing, technology adoption and skill development will create opportunities for the country’s youth and strengthen its position in the global economy. Speaking on Free Trade Agreements, the Minister stated that the US bilateral trade agreement’s first tranche has been finalized and is going through final contours and the legal drafting. He expressed hope that India will  finalize and operationalize the agreement soon, once the country secures competitive advantage over its peer countries.Mr Goyal highlighted that countries are increasingly being assessed as manufacturing and investment destinations on the basis of political stability, resilient supply chains and fair and transparent trading practices. He expressed confidence that India will remain among the fastest-growing large economies over the next 20 to 25 years, supported by its youthful population, demographic dividend, large domestic market and entrepreneurial drive. He noted that Indian professionals are contributing to global businesses, technological development and scientific research, reflecting the growing role of India in shaping the global economic and technology landscape.Mr Goyal also emphasised the importance of continuous learning and personal development, while asking them to view skill enhancement as a lifelong responsibility. The Minister said that India’s youth can play a significant role in translating technological advances into practical solutions across sectors.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is all set to pursue a broader set of capital market reforms to simplify regulatory compliance, improve liquidity in corporate bonds and expand investor access, while retaining safeguards. Addressing the Financial Express Modern BFSI Summit 2026 in Mumbai today, SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator’s priorities included updating listing rules, improving the functioning of debt markets and exploring new technologies to make financial markets more efficient and resilient.Stating that India’s market capitalisation had grown nearly fivefold over the past decade to 472 lakh crore rupees, with more than 15 crore unique investors and 83 lakh crore rupees in mutual fund assets, the SEBI Chairman said regulation needs to keep pace without creating unnecessary complexity.Mr. Pandey said SEBI is exploring an artificial intelligence (AI) sandbox to test applications in a controlled environment, assess risks and develop safeguards while providing regulatory clarity to innovators. As part of its regulatory review, SEBI is also undertaking a comprehensive review of the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) framework and the small and medium enterprise (SME) initial public offering framework to help genuine businesses raise capital while protecting investors.Highlighting the need to improve investor awareness, Mr. Pandey said SEBI’s Investor Survey 2025 found that only 36 percent of investors had moderate to high knowledge of securities markets. The Chairman said SEBI would continue to focus on simpler rules, deeper markets and wider access, while ensuring that technological innovation and market expansion do not weaken investor protection.

. The Supreme Court has sought responses from the Centre and the National Medical Commission (NMC) to a plea seeking greater transparency in the answer key and response-disclosure process for NEET-PG 2026.  A bench of Justices P. S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe issued notices to the authorities and tagged the petition with pending pleas.The petitioners have sought access to the questions and answer options displayed to each candidate, their recorded responses and the correct answers, saying the existing system does not allow candidates to verify their evaluation independently.NEET-PG 2026 was conducted on August 30. A supplementary examination was held on September 5 for candidates affected by a technical disruption at an examination centre in Jaipur.

. Home Minister Amit Shah today extended greetings to the personnel of the National Security Guard (NSG) on its Raising Day. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that the NSG has blown up every terror threat to India with the fury of storms and guarded the nation with steely courage, flawless professionalism and valiant sacrifices.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Canada on the 11th and 12th of December this year. The Indian High Commission in Ottawa, Canada, informed this in a social media post. Recently Prime Minister Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney held a telephonic conversation. During the conversation, both the leaders agreed to build on the positive momentum in ties and work towards concrete outcomes across key areas of the Strategic Partnership. These areas include trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people ties.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact with the Indian contingent that participated in the Asian Games 2026 in New Delhi this evening. The Prime Minister will also address the gathering on the occasion.India finished fourth in the medal tally at the Asian Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, winning 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. This marked India’s second consecutive finish among the top five nations at the Asian Games, reflecting the country’s growing competitiveness across a diverse range of sporting disciplines. India also recorded several notable achievements at the Games, including historic performances in recurve archery, gold medals for both the men’s and women’s hockey teams in the same edition, and maiden medals in soft tennis and mixed martial arts. Other significant achievements included India’s first-ever gold medal in the women’s trap event, a silver medal in weightlifting at the Asian Games after a gap of 28 years, and a silver medal in Greco-Roman wrestling, ending a 64-year wait for an Indian finalist in the discipline.

. The Government has said that India’s merchandise exports to the United States rose to around 51 billion dollars during April-September this year, despite tariff-related disruptions. According to the data released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry, exports to the US were 45.73 billion dollars in the corresponding period last year.Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said that negotiations for the proposed India-US trade agreement are moving in the right direction with both countries working towards concluding the deal at the earliest. The Commerce Secretary said that the growth is supported by higher shipments of electronic goods, petroleum products, engineering goods, chemicals and agricultural products.The Commerce and Industry Ministry said in a statement that India’s total exports for September 2026 are estimated at 80.75 billion dollars, registering a positive growth of 10.99 percent as compared to September 2025. Total imports for September 2026 are around 94 billion dollars, which is a growth of 8.19 percent vis-à-vis September 2025.Meanwhile, India’s total exports during April-September 2026-27 are estimated at 476.20 billion dollars, registering a positive growth of 13.84 percent. Total imports during April-September 2026-27 are estimated at 551.13 billion dollars, which is a growth of 15.68 percent.Merchandise exports during September this year were 44.40 billion dollars as compared to 36.08 billion dollars in September last year. Merchandise imports during September this year were 74.61 billion dollars as compared to 69.08 billion dollars in September last year.

. In the forex market, the rupee appreciated by 10 paise to close at 95.05 rupees against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 102.03 in intra-day trade.

. A two-day national conference on e-Governance reforms will begin today in Dharamshala, the district headquarters of Kangra in Himachal Pradesh. The conference will bring together senior officials and experts from the Central and State Governments to deliberate on various aspects of making governance more transparent, efficient and citizen-centric through digital technology. Union Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda, Union Minister of State Dr Jitendra Singh and Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu are scheduled to attend the conference.The conference is being organised jointly by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, Government of India, and the Government of Himachal Pradesh. Around one hundred delegates from across the country are expected to participate in the event. The conference aims to facilitate the exchange of innovative technologies, administrative reforms and best practices in the field of e-Governance.During the conference, Himachal Pradesh’s initiatives, including Him Parivar, Sukh Ashray, Vidya Samiksha Kendra and Green Himachal, will be showcased. Discussions will also focus on the use of technology in agriculture, healthcare services, judicial administration, digital services and the effective implementation of government schemes.In addition, special sessions will be held on topics such as cybersecurity, data analytics, artificial intelligence and citizen-centric digital services.

. President Droupadi Murmu has accepted the resignation of Dr. L. Murugan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, on the advice of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Rashtrapati Bhawan said in a press communique that the resignation has been accepted under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution.Dr Murugan tendered his resignation yesterday, saying he wishes to return to the grassroots, stand with party workers and dedicate full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.

. Preparations for Durga Puja are nearing completion at temples, puja mandaps and community venues across the country as the five-day celebrations formally begining on Friday, with Maha Shashthi. Major religious venues in the capital, including Dhakeshwari National Temple, Ramna Kali Mandir and Dhaka University’s Jagannath Hall Upashanalaya, are preparing to welcome devotees and visitors. Puja committees across Dhaka and other parts of the country are putting the finishing touches on idols, pandals, colourful lighting and arrangements for religious and cultural programmes.This year, Durga Puja will be celebrated at 33,851 mandaps nationwide, an increase from 32,351 last year.The festival will begin with Maha Shashthi, when devotees perform Bodhan, the ceremonial awakening and invocation of Goddess Durga. Maha Saptami rituals will be observed on Saturday and Sunday, followed by Maha Ashtami on Monday and Maha Navami on Tuesday. The celebrations will conclude with Bijoya Dashami on Wednesday, October 21, when idols will be taken in processions for immersion.The government has extended the Durga Puja holiday to three days through an executive order, providing a five-day break from October 20 to 24 when combined with the regular Friday and Saturday weekend. The Authorities have stepped up security arrangements to ensure peaceful celebrations, with law enforcement agencies strengthening deployments and expanding surveillance at major venues. Officials have also announced measures to facilitate the safe movement of devotees and visitors.Durga Puja commemorates Goddess Durga’s victory over the demon king Mahishasura, symbolising the triumph of good over evil. Beyond its religious significance, the festival reflects Bangladesh’s cultural heritage and tradition of communal harmony.

. The Election Commission has directed 17 States and Union Territories to conduct a Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls with 1st January next year as the qualifying date. These states and UTs are Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal.The Commission said in its letter that it had issued instructions on the 29th of September to undertake a special drive for the enrolment of left-out, young and first-time eligible electors.  EC also said that the schedule for SSR in States and UTs where the Special Intensive Revision is ongoing or has recently been completed will be announced later. It added that for Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, where SIR has not been started so far, the schedule for roll revision will be announced in due course of time.The Commission further said that the Electoral Registration Officer of the concerned assembly constituency shall be responsible for ensuring that no eligible citizen is left out while no ineligible person gets included or remains in the Electoral Roll. During the Special Summary Revision, the Chief Electoral Officer, District Election Officers, and Electoral Registration Officers will ensure that every eligible person is enrolled as an elector.Our correspondent reports that since the revision is a Summary Revision in nature, there will be no house-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers to electors. In order to ensure maximum participation of the young and first-time voters, all prospective electors eligible on 1st January 2027 and those who become eligible on 1st April 2027, 1st July 2027, and 1st October 2027 can also send their advance applications for enrolment. Help desks will be set up at the district level to facilitate enrolment of electors, especially migrants, the vulnerable, and marginalised.

. Ukraine has accused the United States of helping Russia as it fails to provide timely warnings about Russian missile strikes and has raised concerns over Starlink restrictions. The accusation follows massive Russian aerial assaults that killed nine people, targeted power and heating plants, and cut electricity to over 6 lakh residents. The ballistic missiles hit Kyiv before air raid sirens could activate.Ties between Kyiv and Washington have deteriorated after US President Donald Trump lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, urged a halt to strikes on Russian refineries, and suggested replacing Ukraine’s wartime leader.

. Indian wrestler Vishvajit Ramchandra More has created history by clinching a historic silver medal in the Greco-Roman finals at the U23 World Championships in Las Vegas today. Competing in the men’s 55kg final, More narrowly lost 12-13 to Georgia’s Koba Karumidze in the final seconds of the bout.​This marks India’s first-ever silver medal and first-ever appearance in a Greco-Roman final at the U23 World Championships. Earlier in the week, the two-time U23 bronze medallist secured his place in the history books by advancing through a challenging draw.​More opened his campaign with a 10-8 victory over Mexico’s Isaac Marin Mata, followed by an 8-1 win against Iran’s U20 world champion Armin Shamsipour in the quarterfinals using a four-pointer throw. He then defeated Russia’s Malik Gigiev 6-4 in a thrilling semifinal encounter to reach the title match.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has launched the National Strategic Trade Command Centre (NSTCC) in New Delhi. NSTCC is a strategic initiative aimed at strengthening the monitoring, analysis and governance of India’s international trade ecosystem through integrated data analytics and evidence-based decision-making.The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the Command Centre has been conceptualised to provide senior policymakers and government officials with a consolidated view of India’s trade performance, export promotion schemes, regulatory approvals, application processing and operational indicators.It will bring together dashboards covering key DGFT functions and trade-related domains, including Importer Exporter Code, Advance Authorisation, Export Promotion Capital Goods, Certificate of Origin, SCOMET, restricted imports and exports, and other regulatory and trade facilitation processes.Speaking on the occasion, Mr Goyal lauded NSTCC for enabling data-driven, evidence-based trade decisions. The Minister also called for regular meetings of the Inter-Ministerial Committee to clear the backlog of pending applications and ensure that all applications are cleared expeditiously.

. North Korea has said that it has test-fired cruise missiles designed to be fired from submarines. The move comes as Pyongyang continues to expand its military capabilities during a prolonged freeze in diplomacy with Washington and Seoul. North Korean state media said the military tested two types of these missiles in the country’s eastern waters yesterday. However, the report did not specify whether they were launched from an actual submarine or an underwater test platform. South Korea’s military did not immediately comment on the tests.

. Ukraine launched a drone and missile attack on a Russian oil refinery today. Russia’s Defence Ministry said that Ukraine launched a major attack on a refinery in the Ryazan region southeast of Moscow early this morning. It said that air defences downed four Ukrainian Flamingo missiles and 69 drones attacking the refinery, but drone fragments sparked a fire at the refinery. The strikes came hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that a brief energy infrastructure truce spurned by Moscow was over.

. In Men’s Cricket, the West Indies defeated India by 24 runs in the fourth T20 International in Hyderabad last night. Chasing a target of 248 runs set by West Indies, India scored 223 for nine in 19.3 overs. Sanju Samson was the top scorer with 56 runs. Tilak Varma scored 43 runs. Arshdeep Singh retired hurt with 5 runs. For West Indies, Keemo Paul scalped 5 wickets.Earlier, put into bat, West Indies posted 247 runs for the loss of three wickets in the stipulated 20 overs. West Indies Captain Shai Hope scored an unbeaten 102 runs off 50 balls. Shai Hope was adjudged the Player of the Match.The five-match series is now levelled at 2-2. The last match of the series will be played on 17th of this month at M.Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru.

. Major Asian stock markets edged lower today. South Korea’s Kospi index nosedived nearly 7.6 per cent, dragged by chip heavyweights. Japan’s Nikkei 225 tanked 4.9 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex shed 3.4 per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite fell 1.6 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped one per cent, and Singapore’s Strait Times slipped almost 0.4 per cent.In European markets, Germany’s DAX dropped 0.4 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 added 0.7 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended higher today. The Sensex surged 1,534 points, or 2.11 per cent to close at 74,316. The Nifty rose 375 points, or 1.66 per cent to settle at 22,997.The broader market at the National Stock Exchange underperformed the frontline indices. The Midcap 100 index dropped nearly 0.4 per cent, and the Smallcap 100 index shed 1.3 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 27 out of 30 constituent companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Tech Mahindra skyrocketed 4.6 per cent, ICICI Bank gained 4.2 per cent, and Reliance surged four per cent. In contrast, BEL as well as Trent dropped 0.6 per cent, and Hindustan Unilever slipped over 0.1 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 15 out of 28 sectors ended in the positive zone. Among the top gainers, Top 10 Banks climbed 2.3 per cent, Private Banks advanced over 1.8 per cent, and IT jumped one and a half per cent. In contrast, Capital Goods dropped over 2.4 per cent, Power slipped more than 1.8 per cent, and PSU Banks dipped 1.7 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2668 companies declined, 1720 advanced and 203 remained unchanged.

. Global crude oil prices eased today. Brent crude was trading 1.7 per cent down at 104 US dollars and 21 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.2 per cent down at 94 US dollars and 95 cents per barrel.

. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh has urged all Indian nationals to continue to follow local authorities’ instructions, stay indoors in case of an aerial attack, and refrain from circulating videos or news related to ongoing events in view of the current situation in Saudi Arabia. In a fresh advisory, the Embassy informed that two Indian nationals who were injured in the Riyadh airport attack on the 10th of October continue to remain in the ICU. One Indian national has been shifted from the ICU to the High Dependency Unit. Four more Indian nationals continue to receive medical care in a normal ward, and one person was discharged from the hospital.Flight operations continue to remain suspended at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Flight operations at Dammam, Jeddah, and Medina continue, with some disruptions. Indian carriers have suspended flights to and from Saudi Arabia until the 17th of October. Saudia Airlines continues to operate scheduled flights from Dammam, Jeddah, and Medina. Flynas is operating scheduled flights on the Dammam-Lucknow sector.

. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas conducted a special inspection drive in Delhi to assess road dust and effectiveness of road cleaning operations across the city.The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has informed that the commission deployed four flying squad teams for the inspection which was carried out yesterday. The Flying Squad Teams inspected 25 road stretches covering approximately 35 kilometres of the Inner and Outer ring road which come under the jurisdiction of the Public Works Department (PWD), Delhi.The Ministry highlighted that the inspections, which were meant to seek strict implementation of road cleaning and dust mitigation measures, found 17 cases of violation. These violations include accumulation of construction and demolition waste and high visible road dust across inspected road stretches.CAQM has directed PWD, Delhi and other concerned agencies to take appropriate corrective measures to control road dust on priority basis. It also added the inspection shall continue under Operation Clean Air across Delhi-NCR to assess on-ground implementation of various air pollution abatement measures.

. Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan today paid floral tributes to the freedom fighter, Veerapandiya Kattabomman, on his death anniversary. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan said that the valour and sacrifice of  Veerapandiya Kattabomman, who refused to bow to British imperialism and stood in fearless opposition, along with the unwavering resolve he held in safeguarding sovereignty, have left an indelible mark in the history of India’s freedom struggle.He added that the life of Veerapandiya Kattabomman, who rejected the yoke of slavery and fought with patriotic fervour and steadfast determination to protect rights, will forever endure in the hearts of the people, even as generations pass.

. The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited (IRCTC) has signed a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Quality Council of India (QCI) to transform the on-board dining experience for millions of daily rail passengers. The partnership establishes a rigorous, technology-driven, independent third-party audit mechanism to ensure the highest standards of food safety and hygiene across all IRCTC-managed mobile and static catering units.Indian Railways said that under this strategic alliance, QCI will deploy certified professionals to conduct intense, unannounced quarterly and half-yearly inspection cycles. These audits will enforce strict compliance with statutory Food Safety and Standards Authority of India regulations and international culinary standards. The MoU marks a definitive shift toward a transparent, passenger-first future, ensuring every meal served on Indian Railways aligns with elite safety and health protocols.

. India recorded a year-on-year increase in overall labour force participation and worker population ratios in September, while the unemployment rate declined to 5% reflecting an improvement in employment indicators. According to data released by the National Statistics Office (NSO) today, rural labour force participation and employment conditions improved, while urban female participation registered a notable monthly rise.The overall Labour Force Participation Rate increased to 55.5 per cent, with rural areas recording stronger growth, while the urban rate saw a marginal year-on-year decline. Female participation improved over the year, particularly in rural areas, while urban female participation reached its highest level since October 2025.The overall Worker Population Ratio rose to 52.7 per cent year-on-year, while the urban ratio reached its highest level since October 2025, with improvements among both men and women.The overall unemployment rate declined by 0.2 percentage points to five per cent compared with September last year. Rural unemployment fell to 4.2 per cent, while urban unemployment remained broadly stable at 6.8 per cent.

. Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav has informed that India’s Ramsar site tally has reached 103. In a social media post, the Minister said that India continues to strengthen its commitment to wetland conservation, with Sukhna Lake in Chandigarh and Sauj Jheel in Uttar Pradesh becoming the latest additions to the list of Ramsar Sites. Mr Yadav said that this milestone highlights the importance that Narendra Modi government has been laying on wetlands in conserving biodiversity, enhancing water and climate security, and sustaining local livelihoods. He said these additions reaffirm India’s ongoing efforts to conserve its rich wetland ecosystems and strengthen the ecological, climatic and livelihood benefits they provide. The Minister also congratulated Uttar Pradesh and Chandigarh for the achievement.

. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has extended the submission deadline for Stage II of the Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge to 22nd of this month. The Ministry said that the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) 2027, has received an overwhelming response from across the country. It informed that over 1.45 crore attempts have been recorded in the Viksit Bharat Quiz as part of the selection process. The Ministry added that about 5.7 lakh youth who qualified in the Quiz round have moved to the next stage, the Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge, where they must submit a 500-word essay on the MY Bharat portal on the theme designated for their region.The Ministry further advised the youth who have not yet submitted their essays to submit them by the 22nd of this month. It said that the extension gives eligible participants more time to submit their essays and encourages wider participation in this national initiative.

. Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya today inaugurated the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games 2026 at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. The Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports organised the games in collaboration with the Gujarat Government.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Dr. Mandaviya emphasised that traditional and indigenous sports serve as a vital bridge, preserving cultural identity while unlocking new opportunities for global collaboration. The Minister added that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, initiatives like Khelo India are fostering a sustainable sports ecosystem from the grassroots to the international level.Mentioning upcoming international events in Ahmedabad, Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi proposed five key initiatives for BRICS nations to preserve indigenous sports, including creatinga joint multilingual digital archive and integrating traditional games into academic curricula.Designed as a non-competitive platform, the Games brought together delegations from member and partner countries who presented a diverse range of indigenous sports.

. In Pakistan, 34 children and a teacher were killed when the roof of a private school collapsed in Peshawar today. City Police chief Mian Saeed said, the incident occurred in Dir Colony in the congested inner city area. Thirty students were present in classrooms on the upper floor of the Al-Khair School when the roof collapsed. Police said, the roof of the three-storey building was poorly constructed.

. Denmark Open Badminton tournament kicks off in Odense today. Two-time Olympic medalist P V Sindhu will take on Yvonne Li of Germany in the Women’s Singles round of 32 match while Tanvi Sharma will be up against Natsuki Nidaira of Japan today. Sindhu will be joined in the women’s singles draw by compatriots Ashmita Chaliha, Devika Sihag and Unnati Hooda.In Men’s Singles, Lakshya Sen and former world number one Kidambi Srikanth will be in action today in the round of 32 matches. India’s Ayush Shetty will also be in action. In Men’s Doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will be in action. World Championships bronze medallists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand will lead India’s challenge in women’s doubles alongside Rutaparna Panda and Swetaparna Panda.
